intro.en: Eminent comes from Latin e- meaning out and minere meaning to jut; eminere is to stand out above the surroundings, like a peak above a range.
intro.cn: eminent 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 minere（突出）；eminere 意为高出周围，像一座山峰高出整片丘陵。

items.en: Minere means to jut or to project, and gives English prominent and imminent.
items.cn: minere 意为突出或伸出，给出英语 prominent 与 imminent。

items.en: Eminere means to stand out, built from e- plus minere.
items.cn: eminere 意为突出、显眼，由 e- 加 minere 构成。

items.en: Eminens is the present participle, meaning standing out or lofty.
items.cn: eminens 是现在分词，意为突出的、高耸的。

items.en: English takes eminent from eminens, first of hills and then of people.
items.cn: 英语由 eminens 借入 eminent，先指山丘，后指人。

items.en: The noun eminence appears for rank, for a hill and as a title for cardinals.
items.cn: 名词 eminence 用于指地位、高地，也作为枢机主教的尊称。

items.en: Law fixes eminent domain as the power of the state to take private land.
items.cn: 法律把 eminent domain 定为政府征用私人土地的权力。

note.en: Eminent, eminence and prominent share the Latin root minere, to jut; imminent looks almost the same but comes from imminere, to hang over.
note.cn: eminent、eminence 与 prominent 共享拉丁词根 minere（突出）；imminent 看起来几乎一样，却来自 imminere（悬在上方）。

dict_mnemonic.text: eminent ＝ e-（向外）＋ min（突出，拉丁 minere）＋ -ent（形容词后缀）＝「向外突出的」→ 杰出显赫。名词 eminence 显赫、高地，也是枢机主教的尊称 His Eminence；副词 eminently 非常、显著地，如 eminently suitable 非常合适；同根 prominent 突出的、prominence 显著，preeminent 超群的。三类用法：人 an eminent scholar 杰出的学者、an eminent physician 名医；地位 an eminent family 显赫家族；品质 eminent for its simplicity 以简洁见长。法律术语 eminent domain 指政府征用私地的权力。比较级 more eminent，没有 eminenter。注意与 imminent（即将发生的）只差一个字母：imminent 是危险悬在头顶，eminent 是声望高出众人。

intro.en: Emission comes from Latin e- meaning out and mittere meaning to send; emittere is to send out, and the noun names both the sending and what is sent.

dict_mnemonic.text: emission ＝ e-（向外）＋ miss（送，拉丁 mittere，过去分词 missus）＋ -ion（名词后缀）＝「送出去这件事」。动词 emit 发出、排放，名词 emitter 发射体、排放源，形容词 emissive 发射的；同根 mission 使命、transmit 传送、permit 允许、omission 遗漏、emissary 使者。三类用法：动作 the emission of light 光的发射；数量 carbon emissions 碳排放、cut vehicle emissions 削减汽车尾气；信号与发行 first emission of banknotes 纸币的首次发行。常见搭配 emission standards 排放标准、zero emission 零排放、greenhouse gas emissions 温室气体排放。可数：an emission 一次排放，emissions 多笔排放。注意与 omission（遗漏）只差一个字母，与 commission（委员会；佣金）同根不同缀。

senses.title: To send out light, heat or sound
senses.definition: to send out energy such as light, heat, sound or radiation
senses.definitionCN: 把光、热、声音或辐射等能量送出去
senses.example: The old stove emitted a steady wave of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 旧炉子持续散发热浪。
senses.why: The Latin verb joins e-, out, with mittere, to send, so emit is literally to send something outward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词由 e-（向外）与 mittere（发送）组合，所以 emit 字面就是「往外送」。

senses.title: To send out gas or waste
senses.definition: to release gas, smoke or other waste into the environment
senses.definitionCN: 把气体、烟雾或其他废物释放到环境中
senses.example: The factory emits less smoke than before.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂排放的烟比以前少。
senses.why: The same outward sending applies to unwanted substances, so the verb became the standard word for pollution sources.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「往外送」也适用于不想要的物质，于是这个动词成了描述污染源的标准词。

senses.title: To utter or express
senses.definition: to say or express something, especially a sound or opinion
senses.definitionCN: 说出或表达某物，尤指声音或意见
senses.example: She emitted a sigh of relief.
senses.exampleCN: 她松了一口气。
senses.why: A voice sends sound outward as a lamp sends light, so the verb extends from physical energy to human utterance.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音把声音送出去，就像灯把光送出去，于是这个动词从物理能量延伸到人的言语。

intro.en: Emit is e-, out, plus the Latin root mit, send, with the English verb ending -t.
intro.cn: emit 是 e-（向外）加拉丁词根 mit（发送），再接英语动词词尾 -t。

latinIntro.en: Mittere and emittere are recorded Latin verbs; emission came through French.
latinIntro.cn: mittere 与 emittere 是有记录的拉丁语动词；emission 则经法语传入。

definition_zh: 情感；情绪；感情
definition_en: a strong feeling such as love, anger or fear; a state of mental agitation
core_image: 心里有什么被搅动起来，一路涌到脸上
scene: 听到消息，她握着电话半天没说出话。Her voice shook with emotion.
sceneCN: 这里 emotion 是「情感、情绪」（第 1 个义项：强烈的内心感受）；句意是她的声音因情绪而发抖。

senses.title: A strong feeling
senses.definition: a strong feeling such as love, anger, fear or joy
senses.definitionCN: 爱、怒、惧、喜等强烈的内心感受
senses.example: Her voice shook with emotion.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音因情绪而发抖。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to move out, so an emotion is something stirred up inside and pushing outward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「向外移动」的动词，所以 emotion 就是心里被搅动起来、并向外推的东西。

senses.title: A particular feeling
senses.definition: one specific feeling, such as guilt, pride or grief
senses.definitionCN: 某一种具体的感受，如内疚、骄傲或悲伤
senses.example: He could not name the emotion he felt.
senses.exampleCN: 他说不出自己感受到的是哪种情绪。
senses.why: The general stirring can be divided into named kinds, so the same noun also counts individual feelings one by one.
senses.whyCN: 笼统的搅动可以分成分门别类的几种，于是同一个名词也用来逐一计数具体情绪。

senses.title: Mental agitation, in formal use
senses.definition: a disturbed or excited state of mind, often contrasted with calm reason
senses.definitionCN: 心绪受扰或兴奋的状态，常与冷静理性相对
senses.example: The speech appealed to emotion rather than reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演讲诉诸情感而非理性。
senses.why: When feelings are stirred strongly, they can override calm thought, so emotion also names agitation as a force opposed to reason.
senses.whyCN: 当感受被强烈搅动时，会压过冷静思考，所以 emotion 也指一股与理性相对抗的激动力量。

intro.en: Emotion entered English through French and ultimately goes back to a Latin verb meaning to move out.
intro.cn: emotion 经法语进入英语，最终可追溯到表示「向外移动」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Movere meant to move or stir.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、搅动。

items.en: With e-, out, the verb meant to move out or stir up.
items.cn: 加上 e-（向外）后，动词意为移出、激起。

items.en: Esmovoir and later emouvoir carried the sense of stirring feelings.
items.cn: esmovoir 及后来的 emouvoir 带有「搅动感情」的意思。

items.en: The noun named a stirring of the mind.
items.cn: 名词 émotion 指心绪被搅动。

items.en: English emotion settled on strong feeling and later on specific feelings.
items.cn: 英语 emotion 先固定为强烈感受，后又指具体情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emotion family; the near-meaning group separates feeling, sentiment and passion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emotion 词族展开；近义组区分感受、情感与激情。

entries.definition: Relating to or showing emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「情感的、情绪化的」。

entries.definition: In an emotional way.
Arousing strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引起强烈情感的」。

entries.definition: A general word for an inner sensation or attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感觉、感受」，是最宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: A view or feeling, often a refined or expressed one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「情感、观点」，常指较细腻或被表达出的感受。

entries.definition: A very strong emotion, especially love or anger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「激情」，强度高于一般 emotion。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read emotion as movement out of the mind, then let the stirring become a named feeling or a force against reason.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 emotion 读成「从心里往外移动」，再让这次搅动变成具体情绪或对抗理性的力量。

normal.en: E- out plus mov move: something stirred out.
normal.cn: e- 向外加 mov 移动：有东西被搅动着往外走。

normal.en: Strong emotion can shake a voice.
normal.cn: 强烈的情感能让声音发抖。

normal.en: Mixed emotions are several feelings at once.
normal.cn: mixed emotions 就是几种感受同时出现。

normal.en: Emotional is the adjective made with -al.
normal.cn: emotional 是加 -al 构成的形容词。

normal.en: An appeal to emotion opposes an appeal to reason.
normal.cn: 诉诸情感与诉诸理性相对。

abstract.en: Picture a still pond stirred by a hand from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一潭静水被水下的一只手搅动。

abstract.en: The word is movement first and a name for feelings second.
abstract.cn: 这个词先是「移动」，后来才成为感受的名字。

abstract.en: Emotion is weather inside a person.
abstract.cn: emotion 就是一个人内部的天气。

examples.en: Her voice shook with emotion.
examples.cn: 她的声音因情绪而发抖。

examples.en: He could not name the emotion he felt.
examples.cn: 他说不出自己感受到的是哪种情绪。

examples.en: The speech appealed to emotion rather than reason.
examples.cn: 那场演讲诉诸情感而非理性。

root: 经法语 émotion 借入，源头为拉丁语 emovere，由 e-（向外）加 movere（移动、搅动）构成，字面为「把心绪搅动出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Emotion is a stirred feeling in general, then one named feeling, then agitation set against calm reason.
sensesIntro.cn: emotion 先指被搅动的强烈感受，再指某一种具体情绪，最后指与冷静理性相对的激动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something stirring inside a person and rising to the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：心里有东西被搅动，一路涌到脸上。

branches.en: THE STIRRING: strong feeling in general.
branches.cn: 搅动线：泛指强烈感受。

branches.en: THE NAME: one specific feeling such as grief.
branches.cn: 名称线：某种具体情绪，如悲伤。

branches.en: THE FORCE: agitation opposed to calm thought.
branches.cn: 力量线：与冷静思考相对的激动。

branches.en: MASS AND UNIT: the general sea and one wave.
branches.cn: 整体与单数：整片海与一朵浪。

branches.en: FEELING AND POWER: the same stir can move or overpower.
branches.cn: 感受与力量：同一次搅动既能打动，也能压倒。

intro.en: Emotion is a French borrowing whose -ion names a state; its English family adds -al, -ally and -ive.
intro.cn: emotion 是法语借词，其中的 -ion 表示状态；英语词族又加 -al、-ally 与 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Movere and emovere are recorded Latin verbs of moving and stirring.
latinIntro.cn: movere 与 emovere 都是有记录的拉丁语动词，表示移动与搅动。

definition_zh: 情感的；情绪的；易动感情的；令人动情的
definition_en: relating to emotions; showing strong feelings easily; causing strong feelings
core_image: 心里的水面被风一吹，立刻泛起层层波纹
scene: 电影放到重逢那场，观众席里有人轻轻抽泣。The final scene was deeply emotional.
sceneCN: 这里 emotional 是「令人动情的」（第 3 个义项：引起强烈情感）；句意是最后一场戏非常动人。

pos.zh: 情感的；情绪化的；令人动情的

senses.title: Relating to emotions
senses.definition: connected with feelings rather than with pure reason
senses.definitionCN: 与感受有关，而不是与纯粹理性有关
senses.example: Children need emotional support as well as food.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子除了食物，也需要情感支持。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds -al to emotion, so it labels whatever belongs to the stirred inner life.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是在 emotion 后加 -al，用来标记属于「被搅动的内心生活」的一切。

senses.title: Easily moved to strong feeling
senses.definition: showing feelings openly or becoming upset easily
senses.definitionCN: 公开表露感受，或很容易被触动
senses.example: He became emotional when he spoke about his mother.
senses.exampleCN: 谈到母亲时他动情了。
senses.why: A person whose inner water is easily stirred is called emotional, so the adjective also describes a low threshold for feeling.
senses.whyCN: 内心水面容易被搅动的人就被称为 emotional，所以这个形容词也形容感受的门槛很低。

senses.title: Causing strong feelings
senses.definition: producing strong feelings in an audience or reader
senses.definitionCN: 在观众或读者心中激起强烈感受
senses.example: The final scene was deeply emotional.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一场戏非常动人。
senses.why: A scene can stir the viewer the way a hand stirs water, so the adjective turns from the feeler to the thing that makes others feel.
senses.whyCN: 一场戏能像手搅水一样搅动观众，于是这个形容词从「感受者」转向「让别人产生感受的事物」。

intro.en: Emotional is a native English formation from emotion plus the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: emotional 是英语在 emotion 后加形容词词尾 -al 构成的本土派生词。

items.en: The ultimate verb meant to move out or stir up.
items.cn: 最终源头动词意为移出、激起。

items.en: The noun named a stirring of the mind.
items.cn: 名词指心绪被搅动。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The adjective emotional was formed with -al.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，加 -al 构成形容词 emotional。

items.en: It now covers the emotional life, a person's temperament and moving works of art.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖情感生活、人的性情与动人的艺术作品。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emotion family; the near-meaning group separates sentimental, moving and passionate.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emotion 词族展开；近义组区分多愁善感、动人以及充满激情。

entries.definition: A strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「情感」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: In a way connected with feelings.
Arousing feeling, often used of words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引起情感的」，多用于词语。

entries.definition: Excessively tender about memories or love.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多愁善感的」，常带过度感伤色彩。

entries.definition: Producing a strong feeling of sadness or sympathy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「动人的」，强调引发怜惜或悲伤。

entries.definition: Filled with very strong feeling or belief.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充满激情的」，强度更高。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from emotion plus -al, then let the adjective describe the feeling life, the person and the artwork.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从 emotion 加 -al 出发，再让这个形容词分别描述情感生活、人与作品。

normal.en: Emotion plus -al makes the adjective.
normal.cn: emotion 加 -al 构成形容词。

normal.en: Emotional support is care for the inner life.
normal.cn: emotional support 是对内心的照顾。

normal.en: An emotional person is easily moved.
normal.cn: emotional person 就是容易被触动的人。

normal.en: An emotional scene moves the audience.
normal.cn: emotional scene 能打动观众。

normal.en: Emotionally is the adverb made with -ly.
normal.cn: emotionally 是加 -ly 构成的副词。

abstract.en: Picture wind touching a still pond and spreading rings.
abstract.cn: 想象风碰到静水，波纹一圈圈散开。

abstract.en: The adjective can point to the feeling, the feeler or the cause.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词可以指向感受、感受者或成因。

abstract.en: Emotional is emotion given a direction.
abstract.cn: emotional 就是被指明了方向的情感。

examples.en: Children need emotional support as well as food.
examples.cn: 孩子除了食物，也需要情感支持。

examples.en: He became emotional when he spoke about his mother.

examples.en: The final scene was deeply emotional.
examples.cn: 最后一场戏非常动人。

root: 由 emotion 加形容词词尾 -al 构成；emotion 经法语来自拉丁语 emovere，即 e-（向外）加 movere（移动、搅动）。

sensesIntro.en: Emotional describes what belongs to feeling, a person easily stirred, and a work that stirs others.
sensesIntro.cn: emotional 既形容属于感受的事物，也形容容易被触动的人，还形容能打动他人的作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wind touching a still inner pond and spreading rings.
core.cn: 核心意象：风拂过内心的静水，波纹层层散开。

branches.en: THE DOMAIN: what belongs to emotion.
branches.cn: 领域线：属于情感范围的事物。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a low threshold for feeling.
branches.cn: 人物线：感受门槛很低的人。

branches.en: THE WORK: art that stirs the audience.
branches.cn: 作品线：搅动观众的艺术。

branches.en: FIELD AND TEMPER: the general field and a personal trait.
branches.cn: 领域与性情：一般领域与个人特质。

branches.en: FEELER AND CAUSE: the moved person and the moving scene.
branches.cn: 感受者与成因：被感动的人与动人的场景。

intro.en: Emotional is emotion plus -al, an adjective ending meaning relating to.
intro.cn: emotional 是 emotion 加 -al，这个词尾表示「与……有关的」。

latinIntro.en: The -al ending came through French and Latin, while the root movere is recorded Latin.
latinIntro.cn: -al 词尾经法语与拉丁语进入英语，词根 movere 则是有记录的拉丁语。

definition_zh: 有共情力的；体察他人处境的；善解人意的；同理式的；移情的；令人代入的；体谅的；以用户感受为中心的
definition_en: able to understand and share what another person is feeling
core_image: 一个人听人说话时，眉毛先于对方皱了起来
scene: 会议里有人低声说家里出了事，坐在斜对面的同事没有追问，只把会议记录推到一边。When a colleague mentioned a family emergency in a low voice, the woman across the table said nothing and quietly moved the minutes aside, an empathetic response.
sceneCN: 这里 empathetic 指「体察他人处境的回应」（第 2 个义项：以举动体现对他人感受的理解）；句意为同事低声提到家中急事，斜对面的女士没有追问，只把会议记录推到一边，这便是体察他人处境的回应。可辨识物件：会议桌、记录本、推开的动作、压低的声音。

pos.zh: 有共情力的；体察他人处境的；善解人意的；同理式的；移情的；令人代入的；体谅的；以用户感受为中心的

collocations.zh: 以用户感受为中心的设计

senses.title: A person who feels with others
senses.definition: of a person, readily understanding and sharing the feelings of others
senses.definitionCN: 指人容易理解并分担他人的感受
senses.example: She is the most empathetic person in the department.
senses.exampleCN: 她是部门里最有共情力的人。
senses.why: The adjective moves the noun onto a person: empathy is the capacity, and empathetic says that someone has it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词移到人身上：empathy 是能力，empathetic 则说明某人拥有这种能力。

senses.title: A reply that fits the feeling
senses.titleCN: 与对方感受相称的回应
senses.definition: of a response or action, showing that another's feeling has been understood
senses.definitionCN: 指回应或举动显示已理解对方的感受
senses.example: His empathetic reply was to sit down and say nothing for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回应是坐下来，先沉默片刻，这正体察了对方的感受。
senses.why: A response can demonstrate understanding even when no words are offered, which is why the adjective often describes actions.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有言语，回应也能显示理解，因此这个形容词常用来描述动作。

senses.title: A temperament that notices
senses.definition: having a temperament that notices and cares about others' states
senses.definitionCN: 具有留意并关心他人状态的性格
senses.example: The nurses described him as empathetic and unhurried.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们说他善解人意，而且从不急躁。
senses.why: Temperament is the standing version of a single act: what someone does once, an empathetic person does by habit.
senses.whyCN: 性格是单次行为的持久版本：某人偶一为之的事，善解人意者会习惯性地去做。

senses.title: Listening that gives room
senses.definition: of a way of listening that leaves the speaker room to finish
senses.definitionCN: 指一种让说话者把话说完的倾听方式
senses.example: Her empathetic listening kept him talking when he might have stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 她共情式的倾听让他在本可能停下时继续说了下去。
senses.why: The word can describe technique as well as feeling, because listening has a form that can be learned.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可描述感受，也可描述技巧，因为倾听有一种可以学会的形式。

senses.title: The clinical sense
senses.definition: in psychology, relating to the practitioner's entry into another's experience
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，指从业者进入他人体验的做法
senses.example: The training stresses an empathetic stance rather than quick interpretation.
senses.exampleCN: 培训强调共情的立场，而非急于作出解释。
senses.why: Clinical writing needed an adjective for the trained stance, and chose this one over the older variant.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作需要一个形容词来指受训后的立场，于是选用了这个较新的变体。

senses.title: Work that holds the viewer
senses.definition: of a story or image, drawing the audience into a character's feeling
senses.definitionCN: 指故事或影像把观众带入角色的感受
senses.example: The documentary is empathetic without ever becoming sentimental.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片让人代入，却从不流于感伤。
senses.why: Art can lend feeling without claiming it, and criticism uses the adjective for that loan.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以借出感受而不将其据为己有，评论便用这个形容词指这种出借。

senses.title: Considerate under pressure
senses.definition: showing consideration for someone in a difficult position
senses.definitionCN: 对处境困难者表现出体贴
senses.example: The manager was empathetic about the deadline and moved it by a week.
senses.exampleCN: 经理对截止期限的处理很体谅，把它往后挪了一周。
senses.why: Consideration becomes visible when a rule is bent for a person, and the adjective covers that small bend.
senses.whyCN: 当规则为某个人稍作弯折时，体谅就变得可见，这个形容词正涵盖那一点弯折。

senses.title: Designed from the user's seat
senses.titleCN: 从使用者位置出发的设计
senses.definition: in design and service work, based on an understanding of users' experience
senses.definitionCN: 设计与服务工作中，建立在理解使用者体验之上
senses.example: The team ran an empathetic review of the complaint logs.
senses.exampleCN: 团队对投诉记录做了一次以用户感受为中心的复核。
senses.why: Design borrowed the word and made it a method: read the logs, sit in the chair, then build.
senses.whyCN: 设计借用了这个词并把它变成方法：读记录、坐进那把椅子，然后再动手。

intro.en: Empathetic is empathy plus the Greek adjective ending -etikos, and it competes with the older empathic. Empathy itself comes from Greek empatheia, from en- 'in' and pathos 'feeling'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: empathetic 是 empathy 加希腊形容词词尾 -etikos 构成，与更早的 empathic 并存。empathy 本身来自希腊 empatheia，由 en-「在内」与 pathos「感受」构成。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Pathos meant what a person undergoes and the feeling it produces. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for suffering, but the form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: pathos 指人所经历的事以及由此产生的感受。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「受苦」的词根有关，但该形式属重构。

items.en: The noun entered English in the early twentieth century as a rendering of German aesthetic theory, then moved into psychology.
items.cn: 这个名词在二十世纪初进入英语，用以转译德国美学理论，随后进入心理学。

items.en: Empathic follows the shorter Greek pattern; empathetic follows the longer one and became common in clinical and general prose. Neither is wrong, and style guides differ.
items.cn: empathic 依循较短的希腊构词模式；empathetic 依循较长的模式，在临床与一般文章中更为常见。两者都不算错，各家体例偏好不同。

items.en: From counselling the adjective spread to management writing, art criticism and design, often before the response rather than the person.
items.cn: 这个形容词从心理咨询扩散到管理写作、艺术批评与设计，常放在「回应」之前而非「人」之前。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-history of pathos is a reconstruction, and the first English use of this adjective is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：pathos 的早期历史属重构，这个形容词的英语最早用例也无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and two adjectives that look close but mean something else; group two holds words for understanding others' feelings.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加两个形近却另有含义的形容词；第二组是表示理解他人感受的词。

entries.definition: The capacity itself; empathetic describes a person or response that shows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身；empathetic 形容表现这种能力的人或回应。

entries.definition: The older and shorter adjective, common in clinical writing; the meaning is the same as empathetic.
entries.definitionCN: 更早、更短的形容词，常见于临床写作；含义与 empathetic 相同。

entries.definition: From Greek emphasis 'display', meaning forcefully stressed; it has no pathos and no feeling in its root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 emphasis「显示」，意为强调的；词根里既无 pathos，也无感受。

entries.definition: Built on pathos but means sadly inadequate or deserving pity; the prefix, not the root, separates it.
entries.definitionCN: 建在 pathos 上，却意为可怜、差劲；区分它的是前缀而非词根。

entries.definition: Feeling sorry for someone's trouble; empathetic implies sharing the feeling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人的困境感到难过；empathetic 意味着共享那份感受本身。

entries.definition: Pity joined to a readiness to help; empathetic may stay with understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 怜悯并伴随帮助的意愿；empathetic 可能只停留在理解。

entries.definition: Able to see why someone acts as they do; empathetic adds the felt side.
entries.definitionCN: 能看出某人为何如此行事；empathetic 另添了感受的一面。

entries.definition: Quick to notice others' states, sometimes to one's own cost; empathetic stresses the sharing, not the noticing.
entries.definitionCN: 容易察觉他人状态，有时以自身为代价；empathetic 强调共享，而非察觉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root of feeling, the two real adjective forms, and the real settings where the word is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「感受」词根、两个真实的形容词形式，以及这个词真实出现的场合。

normal.en: Empathy plus -etic gives the adjective, just as energy plus -etic gives energetic.
normal.cn: empathy 加 -etic 构成形容词，正如 energy 加 -etic 构成 energetic。

normal.en: Emphatic looks like this word but means forcefully stressed, so the two must be kept apart by their roots.
normal.cn: emphatic 字形相近却意为强调的，两者必须靠词根分清。

normal.en: The older empathic survives in clinical writing; empathetic is the common general form.
normal.cn: 较旧的 empathic 仍用于临床写作；empathetic 是常见的一般形式。

normal.en: It often sits before response, listening, approach and leader.
normal.cn: 它常放在回应、倾听、做法与领导者之前。

normal.en: The adverb empathetically marks how something is done, not what is felt.
normal.cn: 副词 empathetically 标示做事的方式，而非感受的内容。

abstract.en: Picture a brow that folds a moment before the speaker's does.
abstract.cn: 想象一道眉毛比说话者更早皱起。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook pushed aside without a word, because the note can wait.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记录本被无声地推到一边，因为记录可以等。

abstract.en: Picture a chair in a call centre occupied by a designer for one full shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一名设计师在呼叫中心的椅子上坐满一整班。

examples.en: An empathetic teacher notices the student who has stopped asking questions.
examples.cn: 有共情力的老师会注意到那个不再提问的学生。

examples.en: The report recommends a more empathetic approach to complaints.
examples.cn: 报告建议以更体察对方的方式处理投诉。

examples.en: Her empathetic silence gave him time to finish.
examples.cn: 她体谅的沉默给了他时间把话说完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em（在内）+ pathetic（感受的）」——能走进别人感受里的 → 有共情力的

root: 希腊 empatheia（en-「在内」+ pathos「感受」）+ 形容词词尾 -etikos；与更早的 empathic 同义并存。pathos 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one early frown: a person who feels with others, a reply that fits the feeling, a noticing temperament, listening that leaves room, a clinical stance, a work that holds the viewer, consideration under pressure, and design from the user's seat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次提前皱起的眉展开：与他人同感的人、与感受相称的回应、善于察觉的性格、留出空间的倾听、临床立场、令人代入的作品、困境中的体谅，以及从使用者位置出发的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brow that folds a moment before the speaker's brow does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道比说话者更早皱起的眉毛。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE TRAIT: someone who feels with others, and the temperament that makes it habitual.
branches.cn: 人与性格：与他人同感的人，以及使这件事成为习惯的性格。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE AND THE BEND: a reply that fits the feeling, and a rule moved for a person under pressure.
branches.cn: 回应与弯折：与感受相称的回应，以及为困境中的人挪动的规则。

branches.en: THE FORM OF LISTENING: silence that leaves the speaker room to finish.
branches.cn: 倾听的形式：让说话者把话说完的沉默。

branches.en: TRAINED AND BORROWED: the clinical stance, and the story that lends feeling to a viewer.
branches.cn: 受训与借出：临床立场，以及把感受借给观众的故事。

branches.en: DESIGNED FROM ANOTHER'S SEAT: a method that begins with the user's experience.
branches.cn: 从他人位置出发的设计：以使用者体验为起点的方法。

intro.en: Empathetic is the longer of two adjectives built on empathy, which is itself built from Greek pieces.
intro.cn: empathetic 是建在 empathy 之上的两个形容词中较长的那个，而 empathy 本身由希腊语构件构成。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, not Latin: en- 'in', pathos 'feeling', and the adjective ending -etikos. No Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这些构件属希腊语而非拉丁语：en-「在内」、pathos「感受」，以及形容词词尾 -etikos。因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The prefix puts the feeling inside the other person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把感受放进他人之内。

items.example: The root supplies the emotional core.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供情感核心。

items.example: The Greek noun stands behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The older adjective survives in clinical writing.
items.exampleCN: 较旧的形容词仍用于临床写作。

items.example: Her reply was brief and empathetic.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答简短而体察人心。

items.example: She tried to empathize with the caller.

items.exampleCN: 他是个有耐心的共情者。

definition_zh: 共情；同理心；共情性理解；代入；共鸣；体谅；移情（美学）；用户体察
definition_en: the ability to understand and share the feelings of another person
core_image: 两个人隔着一张桌子，一个人说到一半停住，另一个人的手也停在杯沿上
scene: 朋友讲到一半忽然停住，对面的人没有插话，只是把杯子放下，等他把那口气缓过去。When the friend broke off mid-sentence, the other person set down the cup and waited, offering empathy rather than advice.
sceneCN: 这里 empathy 指「共情、设身处地理解并分享他人感受」（第 1 个义项）；句意为朋友讲到一半停住，对面的人放下杯子静静等候，给予的是共情而非建议。可辨识物件：桌子、两只杯子、停住的手、沉默。

pos.zh: 共情；同理心；共情性理解；代入；共鸣；体谅；移情（美学）；用户体察

senses.title: Feeling with another
senses.definition: the act of understanding and sharing what another person feels
senses.definitionCN: 理解并分担他人感受的行为
senses.example: She listened with empathy while he described the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲述失去亲人的经过时，她带着共情倾听。
senses.why: The Greek word meant feeling inside something; the modern noun names the act of entering another person's feeling without claiming it as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词原意为「在内部感受」；现代名词指进入他人的感受，却不把它据为己有。

senses.title: The capacity for it
senses.definition: the ability to take another's perspective and feel with them
senses.definitionCN: 采取他人视角并与之共感的能力
senses.example: Empathy can be trained, though it comes more easily to some.
senses.exampleCN: 共情能力可以训练，尽管有些人天生更容易做到。
senses.why: A single act can also be treated as a capacity, and psychology measures it as a trait.
senses.whyCN: 单次行为也可以被看作一种能力，心理学便把它当作一种特质来测量。

senses.title: The counsellor's instrument
senses.definition: in therapy, the practitioner's effort to enter the client's frame of reference
senses.definitionCN: 心理治疗中，从业者努力进入来访者的参照框架
senses.example: The counsellor's empathy helped the client put words to the fear.
senses.exampleCN: 咨询师的共情帮助来访者把那份恐惧说了出来。
senses.why: The profession turned the everyday capacity into a working tool with rules about when to speak.
senses.whyCN: 这一职业把日常能力变成一种工作工具，并规定了何时开口。

senses.title: Standing in another's place
senses.definition: the mental act of placing oneself in another's situation
senses.definitionCN: 在想象中把自己置于他人处境的行为
senses.example: Reading the diary demanded empathy with a person long dead.
senses.exampleCN: 读这本日记需要代入一个早已逝去之人的处境。
senses.why: The word covers imagination as well as feeling: one can enter a situation one has never lived.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既涵盖感受，也涵盖想象：人可以进入自己从未经历过的处境。

senses.title: Resonance with a work
senses.definition: a felt response to a story or experience that seems to match one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对故事或经历产生仿佛与自身相合的感触
senses.example: The film earns empathy rather than admiration.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影赢得的是共鸣，而非赞叹。
senses.why: Art works by placing a stranger's feeling where one's own already sits, and the noun names that placement.
senses.whyCN: 艺术把陌生人的感受放在自己感受已有的位置，这个名词正是命名这种安放。

senses.title: Consideration in daily life
senses.definition: the practical consideration shown to someone in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 对身处困境者表现出的实际体贴
senses.example: He showed little empathy for the staff who had to reorganise their week.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那些不得不重排一周工作的员工几乎毫无体谅。
senses.why: From a feeling the word extends to its visible form: the small adjustment one makes for another.
senses.whyCN: 从感受出发，这个词延伸到其可见形式：为他人的那一点调整。

senses.title: Feeling into an object
senses.definition: in aesthetics, the projection of one's feeling into an object or scene
senses.definitionCN: 美学中把自身情感投射到对象或景物之上
senses.example: The theory of empathy holds that we feel the weight of the stone we see.
senses.exampleCN: 移情理论认为，我们会感到所见的石头的重量。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century aesthetics used the word for reading feeling into forms, a sense older than the counselling one.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪美学用这个词指把感受读进形式之中，这一义比心理咨询义更早。

senses.title: Designing from another's seat
senses.titleCN: 以他人感受为出发点的体察
senses.definition: in design and service work, the practice of understanding users' experience
senses.definitionCN: 设计与服务工作中理解使用者体验的做法
senses.example: The designer spent a day in the call centre to build empathy with customers.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师在呼叫中心待了一天，以建立对顾客的体察。
senses.why: Modern design borrowed the psychological term and made it a method rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计借用了这个心理学名词，把它变成方法而非心情。

intro.en: Empathy comes from Greek empatheia, built on en- 'in' and pathos 'feeling, suffering'. English took it in the early twentieth century as a rendering of German aesthetic theory. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: empathy 来自希腊 empatheia，由 en-「在内」与 pathos「感受、痛苦」构成。英语在二十世纪初借入这个词，用以转译德国的美学理论。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Pathos meant what befalls a person and the feeling it produces. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for suffering, but that is a reconstruction rather than a proven form.
items.cn: pathos 指降临于人身上的事以及由此产生的感受。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「受苦」的词根有关，但那属重构，并非已证形式。

items.en: Empatheia meant 'feeling in', and Greek used it for strong emotion or passionate involvement. The modern psychological sense is a later narrowing.
items.cn: empatheia 意为「在内感受」，希腊语用它指强烈的情感或投入。现代心理学义是后来收窄的结果。

items.en: German aesthetic theory named the projection of feeling into forms, and English writers translated that term as empathy in the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 德国美学为「把感受投射进形式」起了专门名称，英语作者在二十世纪初把它译作 empathy。

items.en: From psychology the noun moved to counselling, then to art criticism, and recently to design and service work.
items.cn: 这个名词从心理学走向心理咨询，再到艺术批评，晚近又进入设计与服务领域。

items.en: Source uncertain (Greek root and first English date): the pre-history of pathos is a reconstruction, and the earliest English use in the modern sense is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（希腊词根与英语首见年代）：pathos 的早期历史属重构，现代义的英语最早用例也无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root Greek words and one look-alike with an unrelated root; group two holds words for feeling with or for others.
note.cn: 第一组是同根希腊词，另加一个词根无关的形近词；第二组是表示「与他人共感或为其动情」的词。

entries.definition: Built on syn- plus pathos: sympathy is feeling for someone's trouble, empathy is feeling with them.
entries.definitionCN: 由 syn- 加 pathos 构成：sympathy 是为他人的困境动情，empathy 是与他们一同感受。

entries.definition: A- 'without' plus pathos: the absence of feeling, the exact opposite of what empathy names.
entries.definitionCN: a-「无」加 pathos：感受的缺席，正是 empathy 所指的反面。

entries.definition: Tele- 'far' plus pathos: the claimed sensing of another's thought at a distance, not a shared feeling.
entries.definitionCN: tele-「远」加 pathos：据称能远距离感知他人想法，而不是共享感受。

entries.definition: From Old English for leisure or vacancy, with no Greek pathos at all; only the opening sound is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语表示空闲、空无的词，与希腊 pathos 毫无关系；共同之处只在开头读音。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of pity that moves one to help; empathy may remain understanding without any action.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的怜悯并促使人行动；empathy 可能只是理解，不含行动。

entries.definition: A grasp of another's reasons; empathy adds the felt share of their emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人理由的把握；empathy 另添了对其情绪的共同感受。

entries.definition: Disposed to feel for someone's trouble; the adjective of sympathy, not of empathy.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于为他人的困境动情；这是 sympathy 的形容词，而非 empathy 的。

entries.definition: A clear grasp of what is going on, often without any shared feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 对情况的清楚把握，常常不含共同感受。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek word for feeling, the German aesthetic origin, and the real verbs built on the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「感受」词、德国美学的来源，以及由这个名词构成的真实动词。

normal.en: En- 'in' plus pathos 'feeling': empathy is feeling inside another's feeling, not merely feeling about it.
normal.cn: en-「在内」加 pathos「感受」：共情是在他人的感受之内感受，而不只是对其有所感。

normal.en: The same pathos root runs through sympathy, apathy and telepathy, and the prefix tells them apart.
normal.cn: 同一个 pathos 词根贯穿 sympathy、apathy 与 telepathy，靠前缀区分。

normal.en: Empathize is the verb, empathetic and empathic the adjectives, and empathizer the person.
normal.cn: 动词是 empathize，形容词是 empathetic 与 empathic，指人的名词是 empathizer。

normal.en: Counselling uses the noun for a professional skill, which is why it appears with show and lack.
normal.cn: 心理咨询把这个名词当作专业技能，因此常与「表现」和「缺乏」连用。

normal.en: Design work turned it into a method: spend time where the user sits.
normal.cn: 设计工作把它变成一种方法：到使用者所在的位置待上一段时间。

abstract.en: Picture two cups on a table and one hand that stops before lifting.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两只杯子，以及一只在举起之前停住的手。

abstract.en: Picture a diary left open at a page written by someone you never met.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊开的日记，那一页出自你从未见过的人之手。

abstract.en: Picture a stone in a gallery that viewers say feels heavy in the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象画廊里一块石头，观者说看着它胸口会发沉。

examples.en: Good doctors combine technical skill with empathy.
examples.cn: 好医生把技术能力与共情结合起来。

examples.en: His empathy for the displaced families shaped the policy.
examples.cn: 他对流离失所家庭的体谅影响了这项政策。

examples.en: The novel asks for empathy with a character who does terrible things.
examples.cn: 这部小说要求读者共情一个做出可怕之事的角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em（在内）+ pathy（感受）」——走进别人的感受里 → 共情、同理心

root: 希腊 empatheia = en-（在内）+ pathos（感受、痛苦）；由「在内部感受」引申为「共情、同理」。pathos 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pause at a table: feeling with another, the capacity behind it, the counsellor's tool, standing in another's place, resonance with a story, everyday consideration, feeling projected into an object, and design that begins from the user's seat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕桌边的一次停顿展开：与他人一同感受、背后的能力、咨询师的工具、代入他人处境、与故事的共鸣、日常的体谅、投射到对象上的感受，以及从使用者位置出发的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at a table, one hand stopping at the rim of a cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌边的两个人，一只手停在杯沿上。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE CAPACITY: feeling with someone, and the ability that makes it possible.
branches.cn: 行为与能力：与他人一同感受，以及使这件事成为可能的能力。

branches.en: THE PROFESSIONAL TOOL: the counsellor's trained entry into a client's frame of reference.
branches.cn: 专业工具：咨询师受训后进入来访者参照框架的做法。

branches.en: ENTERING ANOTHER'S WORLD: standing in a situation one never lived, and resonating with a story.
branches.cn: 进入他人的世界：代入从未经历过的处境，以及与故事产生共鸣。

branches.en: EMPATHY IN PRACTICE: everyday consideration, and design that starts from the user's seat.
branches.cn: 实践中的共情：日常的体谅，以及从使用者位置出发的设计。

branches.en: FEELING INTO FORM: the aesthetic sense in which a stone can feel heavy.
branches.cn: 感受进入形式：美学义，在那里的石头可以显得沉重。

intro.en: Empathy is built from Greek pieces, and its family covers the noun, two adjectives, the verb and the person.
intro.cn: empathy 由希腊语构件构成，其词族包括名词、两个形容词、动词与指人的名词。

latinIntro.en: These are Greek, not Latin, elements: en- 'in', pathos 'feeling', and the noun ending -eia. No Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这些是希腊语而非拉丁语构件：en-「在内」、pathos「感受」以及名词词尾 -eia。因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The prefix places the feeling inside the other person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把感受放进他人之内。

items.example: The root supplies the emotional core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供这个词的情感核心。

items.example: The Greek noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: She listened with empathy while he described the loss.
items.exampleCN: 他讲述失去亲人的经过时，她带着共情倾听。

items.example: The therapist kept an empathic distance.
items.exampleCN: 治疗师保持着共情的距离。

items.example: Her reply was brief and empathetic.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答简短而体察人心。

items.example: He found it hard to empathize with the manager.
items.exampleCN: 他发现很难对那位经理共情。

items.example: He responded empathetically rather than defensively.
items.exampleCN: 他以共情而非防卫的方式回应。

definition_zh: 皇帝；君主；帝王
definition_en: the male sovereign ruler of an empire; a monarch with this title; a dominant figure in a field
core_image: 高座上的人一抬手，整片疆域都跟着动
scene: 宫殿大门缓缓打开，群臣向高座行礼。The emperor received the envoys in the great hall.
sceneCN: 这里 emperor 是「皇帝」（第 1 个义项：帝国的男性最高统治者）；句意是皇帝在大殿接见使节。

senses.title: The ruler of an empire
senses.definition: the male sovereign who rules an empire
senses.definitionCN: 统治一个帝国的男性君主
senses.example: The emperor received the envoys in the great hall.
senses.exampleCN: 皇帝在大殿接见使节。
senses.why: The Latin source is a commander who gives orders, so the emperor is the one whose command holds an empire together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头是发号施令的统帅，所以皇帝就是那个用命令把帝国维系在一起的人。

senses.title: A monarch with this title
senses.definition: a king or sovereign who formally holds the title of emperor
senses.definitionCN: 正式拥有皇帝称号的国王或君主
senses.example: The emperor of Japan has a largely ceremonial role.
senses.exampleCN: 日本天皇的角色主要是礼仪性的。
senses.why: A title can outlive the power behind it, so emperor also names a rank that may now be ceremonial.

items.cn: emphasis 意为显示、显现，由 en- 加 phainein 构成。

items.en: Emphatikos means expressive or significant, the adjective of emphasis.

dict_mnemonic.text: emphatic ＝ em-（在内）＋ phat（显示，希腊 phainein）＋ -ic（形容词后缀）＝「把意思显示出来的」→ 强调的、断然的。名词 emphasis 强调、重点，动词 emphasize 强调，副词 emphatically 断然地、强调地，反义 unemphatic 平淡的。三类用法：语气 an emphatic refusal 断然拒绝、an emphatic denial 坚决否认、in emphatic terms 用强硬措辞；态度 emphatic about the deadline 对截止日期毫不含糊；结果 an emphatic victory 压倒性胜利、an emphatic win 大胜。比较级 more emphatic。注意与 empathetic（有共情力的）拼写相近但词根完全不同：emphatic 是 phainein 显示，empathetic 是 pathos 感受。重音落在第二音节上。

definition_zh: 帝国；疆域；庞大的企业集团
definition_en: a group of countries ruled by one sovereign; the territory so ruled; a large business group
core_image: 一张地图被同一条边界从海岸连到山脉
scene: 地图上一块块颜色被同一条边界连起来，向远方延伸。The empire stretched from the sea to the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里 empire 是「帝国疆域」（第 1 个义项：由一个君主统治的多个地区）；句意是这个帝国从海边一直延伸到山区。

senses.title: A group of lands under one ruler
senses.definition: a group of countries or peoples ruled by a single sovereign
senses.definitionCN: 由一个君主统治的一组国家或民族
senses.example: The empire stretched from the sea to the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国从海边一直延伸到山区。
senses.why: The Latin source means command, so an empire is the whole territory where one command is obeyed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「命令」，所以帝国就是整套「同一条命令被服从」的疆域。

senses.title: The territory itself
senses.definition: the land and peoples considered as one domain
senses.definitionCN: 被看作一个整体的土地与人民
senses.example: Trade routes crossed the empire in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 商路四通八达地穿过帝国疆域。
senses.why: Command and the land that receives it are named together, so empire also means the map rather than the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 命令与接受命令的土地被一起命名，所以 empire 也指那张地图，而不是统治者本人。

senses.title: A large business group
senses.definition: a very large group of companies controlled by one person or organization
senses.definitionCN: 由一个人或组织控制的庞大公司群
senses.example: He built a media empire from a single newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他从一家报纸起家，打造了一个媒体帝国。
senses.why: A market can be ruled like a territory, so the word for political command extends to commercial dominance.
senses.whyCN: 市场可以像疆域一样被统治，于是这个表示政治统治的词扩展到了商业版图。

senses.title: Supreme authority, in older use
senses.definition: supreme command or dominion, an older abstract sense
senses.definitionCN: 最高的统治权或支配权，是较旧的抽象义项
senses.example: The old chronicle speaks of the empire of reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史谈到理性的统治。
senses.why: Before it named a place, imperium named the power itself, and empire can still mean dominion in formal or literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 在指一片土地之前，imperium 指的是权力本身，所以 empire 在正式或文学语境中仍可表示支配权。

intro.en: Empire comes from Latin imperium, the power to command, and only later names the land under that power.
intro.cn: empire 来自拉丁语 imperium（命令之权），后来才指受这种权力支配的土地。

definition_zh: 经验的；实证的；以观察或实验为依据的
definition_en: based on observation, experiment, or direct experience rather than on theory or pure reasoning
core_image: 一双手在泥地里做记录：结论来自亲手试过、亲眼量过。
scene: 评审桌上摊着一份结论漂亮的报告，有人问数据在哪，作者翻遍附件也只找到几段推理。The claim sounds plausible, but there is no empirical evidence for it.
sceneCN: 这里 empirical 是「以观察或实验数据为依据的」（第 1 个义项：实证的）；句意：这个说法听起来合理，却没有实证证据。场景要点：摊开的报告、空白的数据附件、被追问的作者。

pos.zh: 经验的；实证的；以观察或实验为依据的

derivatives.zh: 以经验为依据地；实证地
经验性的；经验派医生；江湖医生

senses.title: Based on observation and experiment
senses.titleCN: 实证的：结论来自观察与实验
senses.definition: based on what can be observed, measured, or tested rather than on theory alone
senses.definitionCN: 以可观察、可测量或可检验的东西为依据，而非仅凭理论
senses.example: The hypothesis has strong empirical support.
senses.exampleCN: 这个假说有强有力的实证支持。
senses.why: Greek empeiria is 'experience', from en 'in' + peira 'trial'. Knowledge that comes from having been in the trial is knowledge from the test, not from reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 empeiria 是“经验”，由 en“在内”+ peira“试炼”构成。来自“身在试炼之中”的知识，就是来自检验的知识，而不是推理的知识。

senses.title: Medical: a physician guided by experience
senses.titleCN: 医学经验派：靠临床经验治病
senses.definition: in the history of medicine, describing a school of physicians who treated by practical experience rather than by theory
senses.definitionCN: 在医学史上，指依靠实际经验而非理论来治病的医生流派
senses.example: The empiric school trusted observed outcomes over ancient texts.
senses.exampleCN: 经验派更相信观察到的结果，而不是古代典籍。
senses.why: The word entered English in the 1560s in medicine, where 'the experienced doctor' was a real professional label, and the source of empirical.
senses.whyCN: 这个词 16 世纪 60 年代正是以医学义进入英语的，“有经验的医生”是一个真实的职业标签，也是 empirical 的来源。

senses.title: Evidence that can be checked
senses.titleCN: 实证证据：能被别人复核
senses.definition: of evidence, able to be checked by others through observation or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 指证据能被他人通过观察或测量来复核
senses.example: The paper offers empirical evidence from three field sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文提供了来自三个田野点的实证证据。
senses.why: A trial is repeatable. Empirical evidence is what another person could have found by running the same observation, so it is public rather than private.
senses.whyCN: 试炼是可重复的。实证证据就是别人做同样的观察也能得到的东西，因此它是公共的，而不是私人的。

senses.title: Testable by observation
senses.definition: of a claim, stated so that observation or experiment could show it to be false
senses.definitionCN: 指一个说法表述得能被观察或实验证明为假
senses.example: A good theory must make empirically testable predictions.
senses.exampleCN: 好的理论必须做出可实证检验的预测。
senses.why: Peira is a trial that can fail. A claim tied to a test is exposed to failure, and that exposure is exactly what makes it empirical.
senses.whyCN: peira 是可能失败的试炼。与检验绑在一起的说法就暴露在失败面前，而这种暴露正是它“实证”的原因。

senses.title: Research done in the field
senses.titleCN: 实证研究：走出去收数据
senses.definition: describing research that collects data from real cases, surveys, or experiments rather than from argument
senses.definitionCN: 指从真实案例、调查或实验中收集数据的研究，而非靠论证
senses.example: Her empirical work involved two years of interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 她的实证研究包含两年的访谈。
senses.why: The researcher goes into the trial rather than watching from outside. Empirical marks the difference between data gathering and armchair reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 研究者是走进试炼里的，而不是在外面看着。empirical 标记的正是“收数据”与“坐而论道”的差别。

senses.title: Chemistry: the simplest formula from experiment
senses.titleCN: 化学经验式：由实验测出的最简比
senses.definition: in chemistry, a formula giving the ratio of atoms measured by experiment, not the actual molecular structure
senses.definitionCN: 化学中由实验测得的原子比例式，而非真实分子结构式
senses.example: Glucose has the empirical formula CH2O.
senses.exampleCN: 葡萄糖的经验式为 CH2O。
senses.why: The ratio is what experiment gives you; the true molecular count needs further work. So this formula is literally the empirical one.
senses.whyCN: 实验直接给出的是比例；真实的分子原子数还要再做工作。因此这个式子字面上就是“经验得到的式子”。

senses.title: Statistics: probability from observed frequency
senses.titleCN: 统计经验概率：由已发生的频率估计
senses.definition: in statistics, describing probability estimated from how often something has actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中，指根据某事实际发生的频率估计出的概率
senses.example: The empirical probability of rain here in May is about one in three.
senses.exampleCN: 这里五月的经验降雨概率约为三分之一。
senses.why: Instead of a model, you count what happened. The trial has already been run many times, and the number is read off the record.
senses.whyCN: 不靠模型，而是去数已发生的事。试炼已经重复多次，数字是从记录里读出来的。

senses.title: Old use: relying on mere experience
senses.titleCN: 旧义贬用：单凭经验、不懂理论
senses.definition: in older usage, describing someone who relies on experience without proper knowledge, sometimes meaning a quack
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指只凭经验而无正当知识的人，有时含“江湖医生”之意
senses.example: The learned physicians dismissed him as a mere empiric.
senses.exampleCN: 学院派医生只把他当江湖医生看待。
senses.why: Greek empeiria could mean 'mere practice without knowledge'. When theory was the mark of a real doctor, experience alone became an insult.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 empeiria 可指“只有实践而无知识”。当理论被视为真正医生的标志时，单凭经验就成了一种贬低。

senses.title: Philosophy: the factual as opposed to the normative
senses.titleCN: 哲学实然：经验事实对照规范
senses.definition: in philosophy, describing questions about what is the case, as opposed to what ought to be
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指关于“实际如何”的问题，与“应当如何”相对
senses.example: The essay separates empirical questions from normative ones.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把经验性问题与规范性问题分开。
senses.why: What is the case can be observed; what ought to be cannot. Empirical marks the side of that line where observation has authority.
senses.whyCN: “实际如何”可以被观察，“应当如何”不能。empirical 标记的是这条线的这一侧——观察在此有权威。

intro.en: Empirical came into English as a medical word from Greek empeiria 'experience', built on en 'in' and peira 'trial'. The whole family is about knowledge earned by being tested.
intro.cn: empirical 作为医学词进入英语，来自希腊语 empeiria“经验”，由 en“在内”与 peira“试炼”构成。整个词族都关于“经检验而得的知识”。

items.en: Peira meant 'trial, attempt, experiment'. It belongs to PIE *per- (3) 'to try, risk', an extended sense of the root 'forward' — to press forward across something is to risk it.
items.cn: peira 意为“试炼、尝试、实验”。它属于原始印欧语 *per-（第 3 义）“试、冒风险”，这是词根“向前”的引申义——向前越过某物，就是冒它的险。

items.en: Empeiros meant 'experienced in a thing, proven by use', from en 'in' + peira. The person has been inside the trial, not beside it.
items.cn: empeiros 意为“在某事上有经验的、经使用验证的”，由 en“在内”+ peira 构成。这个人是在试炼之中，而不是在旁边。

items.en: Empeiria was 'experience', and in medicine could also mean 'mere practice without knowledge'. That ambiguity later supplies the insulting sense of empiric.
items.cn: empeiria 是“经验”，在医学语境中也可指“只有实践而无知识”。这一含混后来提供了 empiric 的贬义。

items.en: Latin empiricus, borrowed from Greek, meant 'a physician guided by experience'. English took the adjective empirical from this Latin form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 empiricus 借自希腊语，意为“凭经验治病的医生”。英语的形容词 empirical 就是从这个拉丁形式来的。

items.en: Empirical is first recorded in the 1560s in medicine, meaning 'pertaining to or derived from experience or experiments'. The general sense 'guided by mere experience' is from 1757.
items.cn: empirical 最早见于 16 世纪 60 年代的医学语境，意为“与经验或实验有关、由之而来的”。“仅凭经验指导”的一般义始于 1757 年。

items.en: Empirically (1640s, 'by means of observation and experiment') became the adverb of the scientific method. Empirical now contrasts with theoretical and normative.
items.cn: empirically（17 世纪 40 年代，“通过观察与实验”）成了科学方法的副词。empirical 如今与 theoretical、normative 相对。

note.en: The first group is the empiric family plus a common spelling trap; the second collects words about knowledge from evidence.
note.cn: 第一组是 empiric 词族，外加一个常见的拼写陷阱；第二组收“以证据求知”的同类词。

entries.definition: based on experience; also a physician who works by experience, often with a negative tone. It is the older form behind empirical.
entries.definitionCN: 以经验为依据的；也指凭经验治病的医生，常带贬义。它是 empirical 之前更早的形式。

entries.definition: the view that knowledge comes from experience and observation. It is the noun of empirical, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 认为知识来自经验与观察的主张。它是 empirical 的名词派生，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a group of states ruled by one power. It comes from Latin imperium 'command', with no link to peira 'trial'.
entries.definitionCN: 由一个强权统治的若干国家。它来自拉丁语 imperium“命令”，与 peira“试炼”无关。

entries.definition: relating to an empire or emperor. Like empire, it belongs to imperium, not to empirical.
entries.definitionCN: 与帝国或皇帝有关的。和 empire 一样，它属于 imperium，与 empirical 无关。

entries.definition: based on tests deliberately set up. It names the method; empirical can also cover plain observation without a designed test.
entries.definitionCN: 以刻意设置的检验为依据的。它指方法；empirical 也可涵盖没有设计过的纯观察。

entries.definition: based on watching and recording without intervening. It is narrower than empirical and often contrasts with experimental.
entries.definitionCN: 以不干预的观察与记录为依据的。它比 empirical 窄，常与 experimental 相对。

entries.definition: based on personal experience. It is about what a person has lived through, not about public data.
entries.definitionCN: 以个人经历为依据的。它说的是一个人经历过什么，而不是公共数据。

entries.definition: judging by practical results rather than theory. It shares the anti-theory attitude but not the demand for evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 以实际结果而非理论来判断。它同样反理论，但不要求证据。

entries.definition: holding that real knowledge comes only from observable facts. It is a philosophical position built on the same demand as empirical.
entries.definitionCN: 主张真正的知识只来自可观察事实。它是以与 empirical 相同的诉求建立的一种哲学立场。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek en 'in' + peira 'trial', giving empeiria 'experience'; family words empiric, empiricism, empiricist, empirically, experiential and experiment (same PIE root).
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 en“在内”+ peira“试炼”，合成 empeiria“经验”；词族为 empiric、empiricism、empiricist、empirically，以及同源印欧词根的 experiential、experiment。

normal.en: Peira is a trial; empeiros is someone who has been inside the trial — hence 'experienced'.
normal.cn: peira 是试炼；empeiros 是走进试炼里的人——因此是“有经验的”。

normal.en: Experiment and empirical share the same PIE root *per- 'to try, risk'.
normal.cn: experiment 与 empirical 共享同一个原始印欧词根 *per-“试、冒风险”。

normal.en: Empirical evidence is evidence someone else could have collected the same way.
normal.cn: 实证证据，就是别人用同样方式也能收集到的证据。

normal.en: Empirical formula in chemistry is the ratio experiment actually gives you, not the full structure.
normal.cn: 化学经验式是实验真正给出的比例，而不是完整结构。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with empire: imperium is 'command', peira is 'trial'.
normal.cn: 别和 empire 混：imperium 是“命令”，peira 是“试炼”。

abstract.en: Empirical means letting the world have the last word.
abstract.cn: 实证，就是让世界拥有最后发言权。

abstract.en: A claim that cannot fail is not empirical, however confident it sounds.
abstract.cn: 一个不可能失败的说法，无论听起来多自信，都不是实证的。

abstract.en: Experience is what remains after the trial has taken something from you.
abstract.cn: 经验，是试炼从你身上拿走一些东西之后留下的东西。

examples.en: There is little empirical support for the claim that the policy reduced crime.
examples.cn: 认为该政策降低了犯罪率的说法缺乏实证支持。

examples.en: The team designed an empirical study with a control group.
examples.cn: 团队设计了一项带对照组的实证研究。

examples.en: The empirical formula tells you the ratio, not the number of atoms in a molecule.
examples.cn: 经验式给出的是比例，而不是分子中的原子数。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬皮瑞克”——硬邦邦的皮面记录本里全是实验数据，一页页都是验过的 → empirical 实证的、经验的

root: 源自希腊语 empeiria“经验”，由 en“在内”+ peira“试炼、实验”构成（peira 属原始印欧语 *per-“试、冒风险”，与 experiment、experience 同源）；拉丁语 empiricus 指“凭经验治病的医生”，英语 16 世纪 60 年代以医学义借入形容词 empirical。核心是“经亲历检验而得”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of empirical, all one standard: a claim counts only if observation or experiment can support or refute it.
sensesIntro.cn: empirical 的九个义项都遵循同一条标准：一个说法只有在观察或实验能支持或驳倒它时才算数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a notebook of measurements taken by hand, in the field, with results crossed out and repeated.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本在田野里手写的测量记录，结果被划掉又重做。

branches.en: METHOD: observation, public evidence, and field research are three levels of the same demand that knowledge be checked.
branches.cn: 方法：观察、公共证据、田野研究，是“知识必须被检验”这一要求的三个层级。

branches.en: HISTORY: the experienced physician was once a professional label, and later, when theory ruled, the same word became an insult.
branches.cn: 历史：经验派医生曾是职业标签；后来理论当道，同一个词又成了贬称。

branches.en: FORMAL USES: the empirical formula of chemistry and the empirical probability of statistics both turn observation into a figure.
branches.cn: 形式用法：化学的经验式与统计的经验概率，都把观察变成一个数字。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: the line between what is and what ought to be is drawn by whether observation can settle it.
branches.cn: 哲学：“实际如何”与“应当如何”之间的线，由“观察能否裁定”来划。

branches.en: RISK: peira is a trial that can fail; being empirical means stating things so that the world may say no.
branches.cn: 风险：peira 是可能失败的试炼；做实证，就是把话说得能被世界回答“不”。

intro.en: Empirical's family is Greek at the root and Latin in its endings. Suffixes mark the method, the doctrine, the person, and the adverb; the prefixes deny or oppose the empirical stance.
intro.cn: empirical 的词族根部是希腊语，词尾是拉丁语。后缀标记方法、学说、人与副词；前缀则否定或反对实证立场。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin form is empiricus 'physician guided by experience', borrowed from Greek. The Greek chain empeiria, empeiros, peira is the real source and is listed separately in the items.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是借自希腊语的 empiricus“凭经验治病的医生”。真正的来源是希腊语链 empeiria、empeiros、peira，已在词条中单列说明。

items.meaningCN: 以观察或实验为依据的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The conclusion rests on empirical data.
items.exampleCN: 这个结论建立在实测数据上。

items.meaning: by means of observation or experiment
items.meaningCN: 通过观察或实验地（-ly 构成副词，17 世纪 40 年代始见）
items.example: The question can be settled empirically.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题可以用实证方式解决。

items.meaning: the doctrine that knowledge comes from experience
items.meaningCN: 认为知识来自经验的学说（-ism 构成主义名词）
items.exampleCN: 英国经验主义塑造了现代心理学。

items.meaningCN: 经验主义者（-ist 构成人名词）
items.example: As an empiricist, she distrusts pure deduction.
items.exampleCN: 作为经验主义者，她不信任纯演绎。

items.meaning: based on experience; an experience-based physician
items.meaningCN: 凭经验的；经验派医生（比 empirical 更早的形式）
items.example: The empiric tradition favoured bedside observation.
items.exampleCN: 经验派传统偏重床旁观察。

items.meaning: not based on observation or experiment
items.meaningCN: 不以观察或实验为依据的（non- 表示否定）
items.example: The theory makes several non-empirical assumptions.
items.exampleCN: 这个理论有几条非经验的假设。

items.meaning: opposed to treating observation as the final test
items.meaningCN: 反对把观察当作最终检验的（anti- 表示“反对”）
items.example: His anti-empirical stance made the review controversial.
items.exampleCN: 他的反实证立场使这篇评论引起争议。

items.meaning: used in compounds meaning 'empirical and ...', as in empirico-critical
items.meaningCN: 构词成分，表示“经验的与……的”，如 empirico-critical（经验批判的）
items.example: The school is known for its empirico-critical method.
items.exampleCN: 这一学派以经验批判方法著称。

items.meaning: evidence obtained by observation or experiment
items.meaningCN: 通过观察或实验获得的证据
items.example: The court asked for empirical evidence, not opinion.
items.exampleCN: 法庭要的是实证证据，不是意见。

items.meaning: a formula giving the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms
items.meaningCN: 给出原子最简整数比的化学式（化学术语）
items.example: The empirical formula is CH2O; the molecular formula is C6H12O6.
items.exampleCN: 经验式是 CH2O，分子式是 C6H12O6。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 有经验的；经使用验证的

latinEntries.structure: Greek noun, from PIE *per- 'to try, risk'

senses.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了五十个人。

senses.title: To make use of something

senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的使用方法、工具或材料
senses.example: They employ a simple method.

senses.whyCN: 工具像工人一样被纳入使用，因此雇用义扩展到使用事物。

senses.title: To keep oneself busy

senses.example: She employed herself in reading.
senses.exampleCN: 她埋头读书。
senses.why: Time and attention are put to work, so the word can describe being fully occupied.
senses.whyCN: 时间和注意力被投入工作，因此这个词也能描述全神贯注的状态。

intro.en: Employ comes from a Latin word meaning to fold in or involve, which passed through French.

items.en: English borrows employ with the sense of using or occupying.
items.cn: 英语借入 employ，表示使用或占用。

items.en: The word settles into the modern sense of hiring workers.
items.cn: 在近代早期，这个词固定为雇用工人的现代义。

items.en: Employ now covers hiring, using, and keeping busy.

definition_en: the state of having paid work, or the act of hiring someone
core_image: 一份签好的工作合同，意味着稳定的收入
scene: 毕业后她找到了一份稳定的工作。After graduation she found steady employment.
sceneCN: 这里 employment 是「就业」（第 1 个义项：拥有有薪工作的状态）；句意：毕业后她找到了一份稳定的工作。

senses.title: The state of having paid work
senses.definition: the condition of having a job that pays wages or a salary
senses.definitionCN: 拥有一份支付工资或薪水的工作的状态
senses.example: The country aims for full employment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家追求充分就业。
senses.why: The noun names the condition produced by being employed, so it points to steady paid work.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名被雇用后产生的状态，因此指向稳定的有薪工作。

senses.title: A job or occupation
senses.definition: a particular job or kind of work someone does
senses.definitionCN: 某人所从事的特定工作或职业
senses.example: Teaching is her main employment.
senses.exampleCN: 教书是她的主要工作。
senses.why: The state of being employed becomes concrete as the job itself.
senses.whyCN: 被雇用的状态具体化，就变成了工作本身。

senses.title: The act of using something
senses.definition: the formal use of a tool, method, or word
senses.definitionCN: 对工具、方法或词语的正式使用
senses.example: The employment of simple tools saved time.
senses.exampleCN: 使用简单工具节省了时间。
senses.why: The older sense of putting something to work survives in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 把某物投入使用的古老含义在正式写作中保留下来。

intro.en: Employment adds the noun ending -ment to employ, naming both the state and the act.
intro.cn: employment 在 employ 后加名词词尾 -ment，既命名状态也命名行为。

items.en: Employer supplies the verb that English later expands.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 提供了英语后来扩展的动词。

items.en: Employ enters English with senses of use and occupation.
items.cn: employ 带着使用与占用的含义进入英语。

items.en: The noun employment appears for both work and use.
items.cn: 名词 employment 出现，兼指工作与使用。

items.en: Employment becomes a key word in economics and law.
items.cn: 在工业时代，employment 成为经济与法律的关键词。

items.en: Employment now chiefly means paid work.
items.cn: 现代英语中，employment 主要指有薪工作。

note.en: Employment is the state or the job; work is the activity, and occupation is the profession.
note.cn: employment 是状态或工作，work 是活动，occupation 是职业。

normal.en: Full employment means almost everyone has work.

definition_zh: 空的；清空；空洞的
definition_en: containing nothing, or to remove everything from something
core_image: 演出散场后，空荡荡的座椅一排排延伸到黑暗里
scene: 演出结束后，礼堂变得空荡荡的。After the show the hall was empty.
sceneCN: 这里 empty 是「空的」（第 1 个义项：里面没有东西或人）；句意：演出结束后，礼堂变得空荡荡的。

senses.title: Containing nothing
senses.definition: having nothing or no one inside
senses.definitionCN: 里面没有任何东西或人
senses.example: The box is empty.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子是空的。
senses.why: The word points to a space with its contents removed, so the container looks bare.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向内容被移走的空间，因此容器显得光秃秃的。

senses.title: To remove everything
senses.definition: to take out all the contents of something
senses.definitionCN: 把某物里面的东西全部取出
senses.example: Please empty the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 请把垃圾桶倒空。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a verb when someone causes the empty state.
senses.whyCN: 当人造成空的状态时，形容词就变成了动词。

senses.title: Hollow or without meaning
senses.definition: lacking real meaning, feeling, or value
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏真正意义、感情或价值的
senses.example: His words sounded empty.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话听起来很空洞。
senses.why: An empty container has nothing inside, so the image extends to words or feelings with no substance.
senses.whyCN: 空容器里面什么都没有，于是这一意象延伸到没有实质的言语或情感。

intro.en: Empty comes from an Old English word for leisure or vacant time, then shifted to vacant space.
intro.cn: empty 来自古英语中表示闲暇或空闲时间的词，后来转为空无一物。

items.en: Æmettig means free from work or occupation.
items.cn: ǣmettig 意为没有工作、空闲的。

items.en: The sense widens from free time to vacant space.
items.cn: 词义从空闲时间扩展到空的空间。

items.en: Empty becomes the standard adjective for containers with nothing in them.
items.cn: 在近代早期，empty 成为空容器的标准形容词。

items.en: The word gains the figurative sense of hollow or meaningless.
items.cn: 这个词获得空洞、无意义的比喻义。

items.en: Empty works as both adjective and verb.
items.cn: 当代英语中，empty 兼作形容词与动词。

note.en: Empty means nothing inside; vacant means not occupied, and bare means without covering.
note.cn: empty 指里面没东西，vacant 指无人占用，bare 指没有覆盖物。

entries.definition: the state of having nothing inside
carrying or bringing nothing
freed from a duty that others must do
not occupied by anyone
not covered or decorated
with nothing written or marked

normalIntro.en: Empty describes a space with nothing in it, and the verb clears the space.
normalIntro.cn: empty 描述里面没有东西的空间，动词义则是清空这个空间。

normal.en: The room was empty after the show.
normal.cn: 演出后房间空荡荡的。

normal.en: Empty promises mean nothing.
normal.cn: empty promises 毫无意义。

normal.en: She emptied the box.
normal.cn: 她把盒子倒空了。

normal.en: An empty bottle is light.
normal.cn: 空瓶子很轻。

normal.en: Emptiness fills the silent hall.
normal.cn: 空荡充满寂静的大厅。

abstract.en: Picture rows of seats in an empty theatre.
abstract.cn: 想象空剧院里一排排座椅。

abstract.en: See an open box with nothing inside.
abstract.cn: 想象打开后空无一物的盒子。

abstract.en: Think of words that sound loud but mean little.
abstract.cn: 想象响亮却没有内容的言语。

examples.en: The box is empty.

examples.en: Please empty the bin.
examples.cn: 请把垃圾桶倒空。

examples.en: His words sounded empty.
examples.cn: 他的话听起来很空洞。

root: 古英语 ǣmettig（空闲的），中古英语时期转为「空无一物」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers vacant space, the act of clearing it, and the feeling of hollowness.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖空的空间、清空的动作，以及空洞的感觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of vacant seats after a show.
core.cn: 核心意象：演出后一排排空座椅。

branches.en: The base sense is a space with nothing inside.
branches.cn: 基本义是里面没有东西的空间。

branches.en: The adjective turns into the act of clearing.
branches.cn: 形容词转化为清空的动作。

branches.en: The container image extends to hollow words and feelings.

branches.en: Physical emptiness becomes emotional emptiness.

definition_zh: vt. 效仿；模仿（并力求赶上或超过）；与…竞争；（计算机）仿真
definition_en: to match or surpass a person or achievement by imitation, or to reproduce the behaviour of a system
core_image: 少年把冠军的比赛录像一帧帧暂停，照着同一个起跳角度在垫子上反复练
scene: 少年把冠军的录像一帧帧暂停，照着同一个起跳角度在垫子上反复练。He tried to emulate the champion by copying every detail of the jump.
sceneCN: 这里 emulate 指「效仿并力求赶上」（第 1 个义项：以模仿的方式追赶或超过某人）；句意是他通过模仿跳跃的每个细节来效仿那位冠军。

senses.title: To match by imitation
senses.definition: to match or surpass someone by copying what they do
senses.definitionCN: （动词）通过模仿某人的做法来赶上或超过他
senses.example: Young players emulate the technique of the champion they admire.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻球员效仿他们崇拜的冠军的技术。
senses.why: A boy pausing a champion video frame by frame and repeating the same take-off angle
senses.whyCN: 少年把冠军录像一帧帧暂停，重复同一个起跳角度

senses.title: To rival
senses.definition: to compete with someone for the same standing
senses.definitionCN: （动词）与某人争夺同样的地位
senses.example: The two workshops emulated each other for the royal commission.
senses.exampleCN: 两家工坊为争取王室委托而相互竞争。
senses.why: Two looms side by side, each weaver watching the cloth of the other
senses.whyCN: 两台织机并排，每个织工都盯着对方的布

senses.title: To reproduce a system
senses.definition: to reproduce the behaviour of one system on another
senses.definitionCN: （动词）在另一系统上重现某系统的行为
senses.example: The software can emulate an older console on a modern laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件能在现代笔记本上仿真一台旧游戏机。
senses.why: A new machine wearing the mask of an old one so that old programs still run
senses.whyCN: 新机器戴上旧机器的面具，让旧程序照样能跑

intro.en: Emulate comes from Latin aemulus, a rival trying to equal another; aemulari is to strive to equal, and the English verb keeps both the copying and the competing.
intro.cn: emulate 来自拉丁语 aemulus（力求与他人比肩的竞争者）；aemulari 意为力求比肩，英语动词同时保留了模仿与竞争两层意思。

items.en: Aemulus means a rival who tries to equal another, and gives English emulous.
items.cn: aemulus 意为力求与他人比肩的竞争者，给出英语 emulous。

items.en: Aemulari means to strive to equal or to rival.
items.cn: aemulari 意为力求比肩、与人竞争。

items.en: Aemulatio is the noun, meaning rivalry or eager imitation.
items.cn: aemulatio 是名词，意为竞争或热切的效仿。

items.en: English takes emulate as to try to equal by imitation.
items.cn: 英语借入 emulate，指通过模仿力求比肩。

items.en: Emulation names both the rivalry and the copying of a model.
items.cn: emulation 同时指竞争与对榜样的模仿。

items.en: Computing uses emulate for one machine reproducing another.
items.cn: 计算机领域用 emulate 指一台机器重现另一台的行为。

note.en: Emulate, emulation and emulous come from Latin aemulus, a rival; imitate and simulate look similar but come from imitari and similis.
note.cn: emulate、emulation 与 emulous 来自拉丁语 aemulus（竞争者）；imitate 与 simulate 看起来相近，却来自 imitari 与 similis。

dict_mnemonic.text: emulate ＝ aemul（竞争者，拉丁 aemulus）＋ -ate（动词后缀）＝「像对手那样力求比肩」→ 效仿、赶超。名词 emulation 效仿、竞争、仿真，名词 emulator 仿真器，形容词 emulous 好胜的、emulative 效仿的。三类用法：赶超 emulate the champion 效仿冠军、emulate the success of 效仿…的成功；竞争 two firms emulate each other 两家公司相互较劲；仿真 emulate an older console 仿真一台旧游戏机、emulate a system 模拟一个系统。常见 seek to emulate 力求效仿。注意 emulate 不只是照着做，还带着要赶上甚至超过的劲头；imitate 只强调复制，simulate 强调重现条件。拼写上与 simulate 只差开头，与 emulous 同根。

definition_zh: 使能够；使成为可能；启用
definition_en: to make someone able to do something, or to make something possible
core_image: 一把钥匙打开平时推不开的门
scene: 这台新机器让我们能更快完成工作。The new machine enables us to work faster.
sceneCN: 这里 enable 是「使能够」（第 1 个义项：使某人有能力做某事）；句意：这台新机器让我们能更快完成工作。

pos.zh: 使能够；使成为可能；启用

senses.title: To make someone able
senses.definition: to give someone the means or ability to do something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事的手段或能力
senses.example: The scholarship enabled her to study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 奖学金使她能够出国留学。
senses.why: The prefix en- puts ability into the person, so the word names the removal of a limit.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 把能力放入一个人身上，因此这个词命名限制的解除。

senses.title: To make something possible
senses.definition: to create the conditions in which an event or process can happen
senses.definitionCN: 创造使某个事件或过程得以发生的条件
senses.example: Good roads enable trade.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的道路使贸易成为可能。
senses.why: Conditions act like keys, so the word also covers making events possible.
senses.whyCN: 条件就像钥匙，因此这个词也涵盖让事件成为可能。

senses.title: To switch a function on
senses.definition: to turn on a feature or setting in a device or program
senses.definitionCN: 打开设备或程序中的某项功能或设置
senses.example: Enable the timer before you start.
senses.exampleCN: 开始前请启用计时器。
senses.why: A feature that is off cannot act, so switching it on is a technical kind of enabling.
senses.whyCN: 关闭的功能无法发挥作用，因此打开它也是一种技术意义上的使能。

intro.en: Enable joins the prefix en-, meaning to make, with the adjective able.
intro.cn: enable 把表示「使成为」的前缀 en- 与形容词 able 结合。

items.en: Habilis means easy to handle or suitable.
items.cn: habilis 意为易于掌控或合适的。

items.en: Able arrives in English through French, meaning capable.
items.cn: able 经法语进入英语，意为有能力的。

items.en: The prefix en- forms verbs meaning to make or put into.
items.cn: 前缀 en- 构成表示「使成为」的动词。

items.en: Enable appears with the sense of making someone capable.
items.cn: enable 出现，表示使某人有能力。

items.en: The word extends to software settings and social conditions.

note.en: Enable makes something possible; allow gives permission, and empower adds power or confidence.

normalIntro.en: Enable puts ability into a person or situation, so action becomes possible.
normalIntro.cn: enable 把能力放入人或情境中，使行动成为可能。

normal.en: The machine enables faster work.
normal.cn: 机器使工作更快。

normal.en: A scholarship enabled her to study.
normal.cn: 奖学金使她能够学习。

normal.en: Enable the timer before starting.
normal.cn: 开始前启用计时器。

normal.en: The -able ending means capable.
normal.cn: 词尾 -able 意为有能力的。

normal.en: An enabler makes things possible.
normal.cn: enabler 使事情成为可能。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers giving ability, creating conditions, and switching on a function.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖给予能力、创造条件，以及打开功能。

branches.en: The base sense is giving a person ability.

branches.en: Conditions can also make events possible.

branches.en: A switched-on feature is enabled in a technical sense.

branches.en: Personal ability and outward conditions work together.

sceneCN: 这里 enact 指「颁布（法律）」（第 1 个义项：把提案正式变成法律）；句意是议会投票通过了这部新安全法。

pos.zh: 颁布；制定；使生效；上演；付诸实施

senses.title: To make into law
senses.definition: to make a proposal or bill into law
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把提案或法案正式变成法律
senses.example: The government moved to enact the bill before the recess.

intro.en: Enact is en- plus act, from Latin actus, a doing, and agere, to drive or do; to enact is to drive a thing into being done, whether a law, a scene or a plan.
intro.cn: enact 由 en- 加 act 组成，act 来自拉丁语 actus（一次做）与 agere（驱动、做）；enact 就是把一件事推动到真正做成，无论是法律、一场戏还是一个计划。

items.en: Agere means to drive, to do or to act, and gives agent and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、做、行动，给出 agent 与 agenda。

items.en: Actus is a doing or a thing done, the noun behind act and action.
items.cn: actus 意为一次做、做成之事，是 act 与 action 背后的名词。

items.en: English forms enact from en- plus act, first of decrees made valid.
items.cn: 英语由 en- 加 act 造出 enact，最初指使法令生效。

items.en: The verb extends to performing a play or acting out a part.
items.cn: 动词扩展到演出戏剧、扮演角色。

items.en: Enactment names both the passing of a law and the law itself.
items.cn: enactment 既指法律的通过，也指通过的那部法律。

items.en: History clubs and courts use reenactment for doing an event again.
items.cn: 历史社团与法庭用 reenactment 指把事件再做一遍。

note.en: Enact, enactment and reenact share the Latin root agere, to do; react, transact and exact come from the same family with other prefixes.
note.cn: enact、enactment 与 reenact 共享拉丁词根 agere（做）；react、transact 与 exact 出自同一词族，只是前缀不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: enact ＝ en-（使进入）＋ act（做，拉丁 agere，过去分词 actus）＝「使成为已做之事」→ 颁布、上演、落实。名词 enactment 颁布、法令、上演，动词 reenact 重演，名词 reenactment 重演、重现；同根 act 行动、actor 演员、action 行动、agent 代理人、agenda 议程、react 反应、transact 办理、exact 精确的。三类用法：立法 enact a law 颁布法律、enact legislation 制定法规、enact a ban 实施禁令；演出 enact a scene 上演一场戏、enact the trial 演那场审判；落实 enact reforms 推行改革、enact the changes 把改动做出来。被动很常见：the law was enacted 法律获得通过。注意 enact 强调从未生效到生效这一步，implement 强调生效后的执行，perform 只指舞台上的演出。

root: en-（使进入）＋ act（做，拉丁 agere → actus）→ enact（使成为已做之事：颁布；上演；落实）
